label: early original-phase input of c/3/d/l (also 2/v/x), positions 2-5
explanation: Reset-gate unit that fires almost only in the original (input) phase (98% of mass), mostly at positions t=2..5 (peak at t=3); it never fires at t=0 or in the copy phase, and only weakly at <DEL> (2% of mass). It is token-selective: the strongest inputs are c, 3, d, l (rate 20-29%), then 2, v, x (10-14%), with weak q/h/i. Activation is stronger at t=2-3 and drops at later positions; it is much weaker on repeat occurrences of a token (in_first=0 is 0.2x lift). The predicate (these 7 tokens at t=2..5) covers 86% of activation mass on dev but precision is only ~0.6: many such steps stay inactive, and I found no clean context (digits seen, prior trigger tokens, first token, previous token) that explains which ones. A first token that is a letter (r/j especially) helps slightly, and a first token that is a digit hurts.
